statement: A customer-value-driven marketing strategy first decides which consumers to serve through market segmentation and targeting.
validation_rule: Do not recommend a target segment without defined segment evidence or criteria.
source_section: Marketing: Creating Customer Value and Engagement

statement: After selecting customers to serve, marketing strategy specifies how to serve them through differentiation and positioning.
required_inputs: target segment; competitor alternatives; value attributes
validation_rule: Positioning claims must be tied to defined customer value attributes and available evidence.
source_section: Marketing: Creating Customer Value and Engagement

statement: A value proposition states the value the organization intends to deliver to target customers.
validation_rule: Do not treat a value proposition as proven customer value without evidence.
source_section: Marketing: Creating Customer Value and Engagement

statement: Customer relationship management focuses on creating customer satisfaction, engagement, and profitable relationships over time.
validation_rule: Separate observed retention/satisfaction metrics from interpretive claims about loyalty.
source_section: Marketing: Creating Customer Value and Engagement

statement: Net Promoter Score measures recommendation tendency by subtracting detractors from promoters.
validation_rule: Inputs must be percentages from the same survey population and period; result must be between -100 and 100.

statement: Customer lifetime value is the present value of future cash flows attributed to a customer relationship.
required_inputs: future margin/cash-flow assumptions; retention; discount rate
validation_rule: State model assumptions; do not mix inconsistent time periods.

statement: For a constant-margin, constant-retention model, CLV can be estimated from margin, retention rate, and discount rate.
required_inputs: margin per period; retention rate per period; discount rate per period
validation_rule: Retention and discount rate must use the same period; denominator must be positive; assumptions of constant margin/retention must be disclosed.

statement: Average acquisition cost is acquisition spending divided by the number of new customers acquired.
formula: Average acquisition cost = Acquisition spending / New customers acquired
validation_rule: New customers acquired must be greater than zero and correspond to the same campaign/time period.

statement: Price elasticity measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a change in price.
formula: Price elasticity = % change in quantity demanded / % change in price
validation_rule: Use comparable periods/conditions and state whether the estimate is observational, experimental, survey-based, or modeled.

statement: For a linear demand function, the contribution-maximizing price is the midpoint between maximum reservation price and variable cost.
formula: Optimal price = (Maximum reservation price + Variable cost per unit) / 2
required_inputs: maximum reservation price; variable cost per unit; linear-demand assumption
validation_rule: Apply only when the linear-demand assumption is defensible.
source_section: 8.4 Optimal prices and linear and constant demand functions

statement: Contribution per unit is selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit.
formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price per unit - Variable cost per unit
required_inputs: selling price per unit; variable cost per unit
validation_rule: Do not mix fixed cost into variable cost; all inputs must use the same unit basis.

statement: CAGR summarizes the average compounded growth rate across multiple periods; it can mask individual year-to-year variation.
required_inputs: starting value; ending value; number of periods
validation_rule: Starting value must be positive for this standard formulation; state N and period unit.

statement: Industry analysis can examine threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, buyer power, supplier power, and current rivalry.
required_inputs: industry participants; substitutes; buyers; suppliers; barriers
validation_rule: Use as a structured qualitative framework; do not convert qualitative force labels into fabricated numeric scores.

statement: SWOT separates internal strengths/weaknesses from external opportunities/threats.
required_inputs: internal capability evidence; external environment evidence
validation_rule: Keep internal and external factors distinct and evidence-based.

statement: PESTLE provides a framework for investigating political, economic, socio-cultural, technological, legal, and environmental influences in the external environment.
validation_rule: Do not present PESTLE items as causal facts without supporting evidence.

statement: A structured business case approach can organize drivers into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive branches, prioritize high-impact branches, request data, and refine hypotheses as evidence emerges.
validation_rule: Treat hypotheses as provisional until tested; avoid forced MECE labels when categories genuinely overlap.

statement: Net present value evaluates an investment by discounting project cash flows and subtracting the initial investment; a positive NPV indicates value creation under the stated discount rate and cash-flow assumptions.
required_inputs: cash flows by period; discount rate; timing convention
validation_rule: Discount rate and cash-flow periodicity must match; include all relevant project cash flows.
source_section: 9. Net Present Value and Other Investment Criteria

statement: IRR is the rate that summarizes a project based on its own cash flows; the common rule accepts a project when IRR exceeds the required return, subject to known IRR limitations.
validation_rule: Flag nonconventional cash flows or multiple/absent IRRs; use NPV as the primary value criterion when rules conflict.

statement: Payback period is the time required for cumulative project cash inflows to recover the initial investment; it is a screening rule rather than a complete value measure.
formula: Payback period = time until cumulative undiscounted cash flows recover initial cost
required_inputs: initial investment; cash flows by period
validation_rule: State whether cash flows are discounted or undiscounted; do not substitute payback for NPV when value creation is the question.

statement: WACC is the rate of return investors expect from the company and is used as an appropriate discount rate for enterprise free cash flow under the valuation framework.
required_inputs: cost of debt; cost of equity; capital weights; tax assumptions
validation_rule: Use capital weights and component costs consistent with the valuation date and cash-flow definition.
source_title: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies
source_section: Core Valuation Principles / Cost of Capital

statement: Productivity measures output relative to input.
validation_rule: Use consistent units and clearly label single-factor versus multifactor productivity.

statement: Capacity utilization is actual output divided by design capacity.
validation_rule: Actual output and design capacity must refer to the same period and output unit.

statement: Forecasts are imperfect; managers should monitor forecast errors for magnitude and nonrandom patterns rather than assuming forecast output is exact.
required_inputs: forecast values; actual values; time period
validation_rule: Compare actual and forecast at the same grain; inspect bias/pattern as well as average error.

statement: The break-even point is the output volume where total cost equals total revenue; below it there is a loss and above it there is profit under the model assumptions.
formula: Break-even volume = Fixed costs / (Price per unit - Variable cost per unit)
required_inputs: fixed cost; selling price per unit; variable cost per unit
validation_rule: Contribution per unit must be positive; cost and price assumptions must be valid for the analyzed volume range.

statement: Inventory turnover measures, on average, how many times inventory is replaced over a period.
required_inputs: inventory usage/sales measure; average inventory; period
validation_rule: State the exact numerator/denominator convention used and keep periods consistent.

statement: A reorder point is the lowest amount of an item on hand and on order before replenishment is triggered in an independent-demand order-point system.
required_inputs: demand; lead time; on-hand/on-order policy; safety stock if used
validation_rule: Use the organization's approved reorder-point formula and matching demand/lead-time units.

statement: Safety stock is buffer inventory used to cover uncertainty such as lead-time variation or defects, but excessive safety stock consumes money and space.
required_inputs: demand uncertainty; lead-time uncertainty; service target
validation_rule: Do not increase safety stock as a default fix without quantifying uncertainty and carrying cost.

statement: EOQ balances inventory carrying cost and ordering/purchasing cost to identify an economical replenishment quantity under its assumptions.
required_inputs: annual demand; ordering cost; carrying cost rate/cost
validation_rule: Verify EOQ assumptions before use; document the cost basis and demand period.

statement: Customer journey mapping analyzes the customer's end-to-end experience and touchpoints so service issues and improvement opportunities can be identified.
required_inputs: persona/user role; journey stages; touchpoints; evidence
validation_rule: Do not infer customer emotions or pain points without observed/reported evidence.

statement: A service blueprint links customer-facing front-stage elements to supporting back-stage processes, data, roles, physical items, measures, and applications.
required_inputs: customer journey; front-stage touchpoints; supporting processes/data/roles
validation_rule: Validate the blueprint with stakeholders and keep front-stage/back-stage dependencies explicit.

statement: Risk culture is reinforced through the behavior of individuals toward risk management; tools, processes, information, engagement, and accountability influence whether risk management becomes routine practice.
required_inputs: risk behaviors; management expectations; process evidence
validation_rule: Do not infer culture solely from policy documents; use behavioral/operational evidence where available.

statement: Key risk indicators are metrics used to support risk management, mitigation, decision making, and strategic planning when designed and integrated appropriately.
required_inputs: defined risk; indicator; threshold/tolerance; monitoring period
validation_rule: An indicator must be connected to a defined risk and decision threshold; do not treat any KPI as a KRI automatically.

statement: Defining risk tolerance supports aligned decision making by clarifying how much variation or exposure is acceptable relative to objectives.
validation_rule: State the owner, measure, threshold, and period; do not invent tolerance levels.
source_section: Risk Appetite and Tolerance / Operational Risk

statement: Analytical SQL should retrieve only the rows and columns needed for the question using explicit SELECT expressions and appropriate filters.
validation_rule: Avoid SELECT * in production analytics unless every column is explicitly required.

statement: Joins combine rows from multiple tables and are foundational for relational analytics.
validation_rule: Validate join keys and expected cardinality to prevent row multiplication.

statement: When aggregate functions and GROUP BY are used, nonaggregated selected columns should be included in the grouping keys under standard SQL semantics.
validation_rule: Reject ambiguous aggregation that relies on permissive nonstandard grouping behavior.

statement: Window functions calculate values over defined row partitions while retaining row-level detail, which is useful for rankings, running calculations, and report-style analytics.
required_inputs: partition keys; order keys; window frame if needed
validation_rule: Define partition/order semantics explicitly and validate against a simpler reference query for critical metrics.

statement: NULL represents missing/unknown values in SQL and must be handled explicitly in filters and calculations.
validation_rule: Use IS NULL/IS NOT NULL or approved NULL-handling functions; do not compare NULL with ordinary equality.

statement: A star schema organizes analytical data into fact and dimension tables to support intuitive filtering, joining, and aggregation.
validation_rule: Define fact-table grain before aggregating; ensure dimensions join on valid keys.
source_section: Loading data into the star schema

statement: Normalized models prioritize transactional integrity, while dimensional models simplify analytical querying; the model should fit the workload.
required_inputs: workload type; integrity needs; analytical needs
validation_rule: Do not denormalize source-of-record data merely to simplify one query; use approved analytical views/models.

statement: Query plans should be inspected when performance matters because scan type, index use, and rows examined reveal how the database intends to execute a query.
validation_rule: Use EXPLAIN/plan inspection without executing destructive changes through the agent.

statement: MySQL EXPLAIN exposes estimated access methods and rows examined, helping diagnose inefficient queries.
validation_rule: Use for diagnosis; do not automatically add/drop indexes from the runtime agent.

statement: Appropriate indexes can reduce the amount of data MySQL must examine for selective queries, but an index does not guarantee a query will read few rows.
required_inputs: filter/join columns; query plan; table size
validation_rule: Assess index benefit from actual workload and EXPLAIN; avoid speculative schema changes in read-only runtime.

statement: Rows examined and rows returned are useful query-cost indicators; a large gap can signal unnecessary work, though joins and workload context matter.
formula: Efficiency indicator = Rows returned / Rows examined
validation_rule: Do not treat the ratio as a universal pass/fail threshold; interpret with access type and query purpose.

statement: pandas groupby supports split-apply-combine analysis: split data by keys, apply summaries or transformations, and combine results.
validation_rule: Grouping keys and output grain must match the business question.

statement: Grouped Python analysis can compute counts, means, standard deviations, rankings, quantiles, transformations, and custom group functions.
validation_rule: Use deterministic functions and document treatment of missing values/outliers.

statement: DataFrame merge/join operations should use explicit keys and known relationship cardinality to avoid accidental duplication.
required_inputs: left/right datasets; join keys; expected cardinality
validation_rule: Check pre/post row counts and duplicate keys for critical joins.
source_section: Data Wrangling: Join, Combine, and Reshape

statement: Missing data must be identified and handled deliberately rather than silently converted into ordinary values.
validation_rule: State whether rows are dropped, imputed, or preserved; never impute business facts without an approved rule.

statement: Pivot tables and cross-tabulations summarize values across categorical dimensions and can support management reporting when the grain is explicit.
required_inputs: verified DataFrame; row dimensions; column dimensions; measure
validation_rule: Check totals against the unpivoted source result.

statement: Data governance specifies decision rights and accountability to ensure appropriate behavior in the valuation, creation, storage, use, archiving, and deletion of data.
validation_rule: Assign accountable owners for governed data and controls; do not rely on the model as governance authority.

statement: Metadata describes data and supports understanding, management, and controlled use of data assets.
validation_rule: Keep schema metadata synchronized with the actual database rather than cached model assumptions.

statement: Data quality must be assessed relative to intended use; analytical outputs are only as reliable as the underlying data and transformations.
required_inputs: data fields; business rules; intended use
validation_rule: Run approved completeness/validity/consistency checks before relying on critical metrics.

statement: Quality checks should occur throughout development, including requirement validation, unit tests, static analysis, local automated tests, CI tests, and security testing.
validation_rule: Do not postpone security/validation testing until the final demo.

statement: Unit tests provide fast feedback on deterministic components and should accompany implementation changes.
required_inputs: function behavior; expected cases; edge cases
validation_rule: Tests must include failure and boundary cases, not only happy paths.

statement: Linting/static analysis and secret scanning provide early feedback before code reaches later test stages.
validation_rule: Review findings; do not blindly auto-fix security-sensitive code.

statement: LLM token selection includes randomness controlled in part by temperature; lower temperature is appropriate when reproducibility and constrained business outputs matter.
validation_rule: Keep production temperature low and verify outputs structurally; low temperature does not guarantee factual correctness.

statement: Structured-output parsers can constrain model responses into defined fields, reducing ambiguity between planning text and executable parameters.
validation_rule: Reject malformed output rather than guessing missing executable fields.

statement: Providing representative examples can improve task accuracy compared with zero-shot prompting for some tasks, but examples do not replace deterministic validation.
validation_rule: Use small, representative examples and still validate every executable field.

statement: For a total-revenue question, aggregate the approved revenue measure over the requested filters in SQL, then validate the scalar result.
validation_rule: Confirm the revenue definition and date/status filters before execution.

statement: For monthly/weekly/daily revenue, aggregate the approved revenue measure at the requested time grain in SQL and return one row per period.
formula: Period revenue = SUM(revenue) GROUP BY requested period
required_inputs: revenue expression; date field; time grain; filters
validation_rule: Check that each record belongs to exactly one requested period and periods are ordered chronologically.

statement: Calculate period-over-period growth deterministically after retrieving verified period totals.
required_inputs: current period value; previous period value
validation_rule: Previous value must be nonzero; periods must be comparable and adjacent under the requested definition.

statement: Use CAGR only for multi-period compounded growth and disclose that it can mask individual year-to-year variation.
required_inputs: starting value; ending value; N periods
validation_rule: Starting value must be positive for the standard formula; state N and unit.

statement: For top products/customers/categories, aggregate the target measure at the entity grain and rank descending; apply a deterministic tie rule.
validation_rule: Verify the aggregation grain and tie-handling; do not rank raw transaction rows.

statement: Average order value should be computed from verified order-level revenue divided by the count of included orders, not from an average of line-item values.
formula: AOV = Total included order revenue / Included order count
validation_rule: Build/verify order grain first; denominator must be nonzero.

statement: Compute an entity contribution share by dividing its verified measure by the verified total for the same scope.
validation_rule: Numerator and denominator must use identical filters/time scope; total must be nonzero.

statement: Calculate NPS from survey classifications only when promoter and detractor percentages are available for the same population.
validation_rule: Result must be within -100 to 100; do not infer NPS from ratings without the defined classification rule.

statement: Use the constant-retention CLV formula only when its assumptions fit the requested analysis.
validation_rule: Same time unit; valid denominator; disclose constant-margin/retention assumptions.

statement: Compute average acquisition cost as total acquisition spending divided by newly acquired customers for the same campaign/period.
formula: AAC = Acquisition spending / New customers acquired
validation_rule: Acquired customer count > 0 and scope aligned.

statement: Estimate price elasticity from comparable percentage changes in quantity demanded and price when the data support such an inference.
required_inputs: price observations; quantity observations; comparable context
validation_rule: Do not infer causality from uncontrolled before/after data; disclose estimation basis.

statement: For a defensible linear-demand model, compute contribution-maximizing price as the midpoint between maximum reservation price and variable cost.
validation_rule: Use only for a linear demand function; otherwise mark method unsupported.

statement: Use contribution per unit to separate variable economics from fixed costs.
required_inputs: price per unit; variable cost per unit
validation_rule: Inputs must use the same unit and currency basis.

statement: Compute break-even volume from fixed cost and positive contribution per unit under constant cost/price assumptions.
formula: Break-even volume = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost)
required_inputs: fixed cost; unit price; unit variable cost
validation_rule: Contribution per unit must be > 0; disclose model assumptions.

statement: Discount each project cash flow at the required rate for its period and sum, including the initial investment.
validation_rule: Rate and cash-flow periods must align; include t=0 correctly.

statement: Compute IRR deterministically as a root of the NPV function, while checking for nonconventional cash flows and ambiguous roots.
validation_rule: If multiple sign changes or no stable root, flag IRR as ambiguous/unavailable and prioritize NPV.

statement: Compute productivity as output divided by the chosen input; state whether the measure is labor, machine, material, or multifactor productivity.
validation_rule: Numerator/denominator must use compatible scope and period; denominator > 0.

statement: Compute utilization as actual output divided by design capacity for the same period.
validation_rule: Design capacity > 0 and same output/time unit.

statement: Calculate inventory turnover using the organization's approved numerator/average-inventory convention and state that convention.
validation_rule: Do not compare turnover values computed with different conventions or periods.

statement: Use the approved reorder-point policy for independent-demand items and include safety stock when the selected policy requires it.
required_inputs: demand rate; lead time; safety stock/policy
validation_rule: Demand and lead-time units must align; never invent safety stock.

statement: For exploratory numeric summaries, use deterministic counts, central tendency, dispersion, quantiles, and grouped summaries before explanatory conclusions.
validation_rule: Report missing-value handling and avoid extrapolating beyond observed data.

statement: Use root-cause methods to investigate why a problem occurs after the problem is evidenced; do not label the first plausible explanation as the root cause.
validation_rule: Require evidence that discriminates among candidate causes.

statement: For external-environment questions, organize evidence under PESTLE categories and keep the output qualitative unless measured data are available.
validation_rule: No fabricated force scores; label dated/geographic evidence.

statement: For industry-structure questions, organize evidence around entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power, and rivalry.
validation_rule: Do not translate narrative evidence into numeric attractiveness scores unless an approved scoring model is provided.

statement: When a business query is unexpectedly slow, inspect EXPLAIN/access type and rows examined before proposing optimization.
validation_rule: Runtime may diagnose but must not alter schema/indexes automatically.

statement: Use a line chart for ordered time trends when the primary question concerns change over time; keep the underlying table available for audit.
validation_rule: Periods must be sorted and complete/explicitly missing; chart values must match the verified table.
source_section: Choosing an effective visual / explanatory analysis

statement: Use a bar chart for discrete category comparisons when length comparison communicates the result more clearly than a table.
validation_rule: Sort intentionally when useful; preserve exact values in supporting table.

statement: After exploratory analysis, communicate the decision-relevant message rather than dumping every tested view.
validation_rule: Every headline statement must be supported by displayed or auditable evidence.
source_section: Exploratory vs. explanatory analysis / Big Idea

statement: Define strict action boundaries so the agent operates only within approved operational constraints.
required_inputs: allowed actions; denied actions; tool permissions
validation_rule: Denied actions remain denied even if requested by prompt or model output.

statement: Critical agent decisions should pass deterministic or rule-based verification before external action or execution.
required_inputs: proposed action; policy constraints; validation result
validation_rule: No executable action proceeds when verification fails or is indeterminate.

statement: Agent autonomy should remain within designer/operator boundaries and does not imply absence of human oversight.
validation_rule: Escalate unsupported/high-risk cases rather than extending autonomous scope.

statement: Prompt injection can manipulate an agent into unsafe instructions; input text must never be treated as authority over system controls.
validation_rule: Security policy and tool validator take precedence over prompt content.

statement: Model output should be filtered and validated against business rules and safety constraints before use.
validation_rule: Reject invalid/unsafe fields instead of repairing them by assumption.

statement: Restrict agent access through authentication and role-based permissions so each runtime path has only the privileges it requires.
validation_rule: Business-query account must not have data-modification/admin privileges.

statement: Apply rate/resource limits to reduce abuse and prevent unbounded model or database workload.
required_inputs: request limits; row limit; timeout; retry limit
validation_rule: Enforce deterministic limits before/around execution.

statement: Log model/tool interactions and security-relevant outcomes sufficiently to detect suspicious patterns and support investigation.
required_inputs: run id; request; tool action; validation status; timestamp
validation_rule: Never log passwords, API secrets, `.env` contents, or hidden chain-of-thought.

statement: Isolate agent operations so unintended behavior cannot spill into broader systems.
required_inputs: approved tools; file paths; process permissions
validation_rule: No arbitrary shell/Python execution from user text; restrict report/output paths.

statement: Use adversarial testing to probe prompt injection, jailbreaks, misuse, and edge-case failure modes in addition to ordinary functional tests.
validation_rule: Security test passes only when unsafe action/data disclosure is blocked deterministically.

statement: Security testing and secret scanning should be performed early in development, not only at final review.
required_inputs: source code; dependency set; commit/test workflow
validation_rule: Review scanner findings and prevent secrets from entering version control.

statement: Business-data SQL must contain exactly one statement.
validation_rule: Reject multiple statements, stacked queries, and statement separators that produce more than one parse tree.

statement: Business-query execution permits read-only SELECT statements only.
validation_rule: Reject INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, CREATE, TRUNCATE, GRANT, REVOKE, CALL, and other non-SELECT statements.

statement: SQL should reference only approved real tables/views and columns discovered from the actual schema.
validation_rule: Reject unknown or disallowed identifiers rather than letting the model guess.

statement: Read-only queries must still be bounded by configured row/resource/time limits.
validation_rule: Apply LIMIT/timeout policy where practical; reject intentionally unbounded extraction.

statement: Use separate least-privileged connections for business reads and application/audit persistence.
validation_rule: Never run normal agent queries as root or a broad administrative account.

statement: Credentials belong in environment configuration and must not be hard-coded, printed, sent to the model, written to reports, or committed to Git.
validation_rule: Redact secret values in exceptions and audit records.

statement: Production LLM inference must use only the configured local Ollama endpoint and must not silently fall back to cloud providers.
validation_rule: When local-only is enabled, allow only localhost/127.0.0.1 approved Ollama hosts.

statement: Do not transmit project database contents, prompts containing sensitive data, or credentials to external LLM endpoints.
validation_rule: Block nonlocal model hosts in production and keep external token billing at zero.

statement: Generated reports and files must remain inside approved output directories using sanitized filenames.
validation_rule: Resolve path and verify it remains under approved base; reject `..`, absolute escape paths, and equivalent traversal.

statement: Audit records should capture decisions, SQL, validation status, and results metadata but not hidden chain-of-thought.
validation_rule: Store concise reason/status codes, not private reasoning traces.

statement: If the local model is unavailable, fail safely with a controlled unavailable status instead of bypassing local-only policy or inventing an answer.
validation_rule: No automatic cloud fallback; no fabricated completion.

statement: Agent retries must be bounded to avoid loops and repeated unsafe/expensive attempts.
validation_rule: Maximum two controlled retries; security failures are not retried by weakening controls.

statement: Hallucinations are more dangerous in agentic systems because incorrect generated information can influence real actions; execution therefore requires verification.
validation_rule: Do not execute an action or report a numerical fact solely because the model states it confidently.

statement: Dividing a market into meaningful customer groups to support selection of customers to serve.
Selecting the customer segment or segments the organization intends to serve.
Defining how an offering should be perceived relative to alternatives in the minds of target customers.
The value the organization promises to deliver to its target customer.
Net Promoter Score: percentage of promoters minus percentage of detractors.
validation_rule: Result range: -100 to 100.

statement: Customer Lifetime Value: present value of future cash flows attributed to the customer relationship.
Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a percentage change in price.
Net Present Value: discounted value of project cash flows including the initial investment.
Internal Rate of Return: a discount rate at which a project NPV is zero.
Weighted Average Cost of Capital: weighted required return across financing sources, used as a discount rate for appropriate enterprise cash flows.
source_title: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies

statement: Output produced relative to input consumed.
Actual output relative to design capacity.
The inventory level at which replenishment is triggered under an order-point policy.
Buffer inventory maintained to cover uncertainty such as lead-time variation or defects.
Economic Order Quantity: replenishment quantity selected by balancing relevant ordering and carrying costs under model assumptions.
Framework separating internal strengths and weaknesses from external opportunities and threats.
Framework for political, economic, socio-cultural, technological, legal, and environmental external influences.
Industry-structure framework covering new entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power, and rivalry.
A representation of a customer's experience across stages and touchpoints of a service.
A model linking front-stage customer interactions with back-stage processes, data, roles, measures, physical items, and applications.
Decision rights and accountability framework governing appropriate data behavior across its lifecycle.
Data that describes or provides context for other data assets.
Analytical model centered on fact tables linked to dimension tables.
A table holding measurable events at a declared grain, typically linked to dimensions by keys.
source_title: Data Modeling with Microsoft Power BI

statement: A table providing descriptive context used to filter, group, or label facts.
source_title: Data Modeling with Microsoft Power BI

statement: The level of detail represented by one row of an analytical fact/result set.
SQL operation that forms groups of rows so aggregate functions can return values at a defined grouping grain.
SQL function evaluated over a defined window/partition of rows while retaining row-level output.
Database structure used to support more efficient row access for suitable query predicates/orderings.
Database query-plan inspection used to understand how a SQL statement is expected to access data.
Adversarial or untrusted instructions intended to manipulate a model/agent into ignoring intended controls or performing unsafe behavior.
Generated content that is unsupported, fabricated, or incorrect relative to required evidence; in agentic systems it can be especially risky when linked to actions.
Model output constrained to a defined field/schema structure for reliable downstream parsing.
Granting only the permissions required for an identity or runtime function to perform its approved task.
D.A.T.A.: Diagnose, Assemble, Take Action, Assess — the controlled execution workflow used by the single runtime agent.
Completion standard requiring verified MySQL evidence, validated SQL/calculations, concise evidence-based response, audit record, and requested report without modifying source business data.
Production LLM inference routed only to the approved localhost Ollama runtime, with no external metered LLM API fallback.
Accept only one parsed SQL statement for a business-data request.
validation_rule: Statement count must equal 1.

statement: Accept only read-only SELECT business queries.
validation_rule: Root statement must be SELECT/read-only; forbidden statement classes must be absent.

statement: Every referenced table/view and column must resolve against approved live schema metadata.
validation_rule: Reject unknown/disallowed identifiers.

statement: Business query output must obey configured maximum-row/resource limits.
validation_rule: Query/result must not exceed configured cap; use deterministic truncation/limit policy.

statement: Aggregated SELECT columns must be aggregated or included in the grouping definition under standard semantics.
validation_rule: Reject ambiguous grouping that can return indeterminate values.

statement: Critical joins must have expected key cardinality and must not silently multiply fact rows.
required_inputs: join keys; pre/post counts; duplicate-key check
validation_rule: Compare row counts and duplicate-key diagnostics at expected grain.

statement: Null values must be handled according to metric semantics rather than silently coerced.
validation_rule: Document exclusion/imputation/preservation rule; reject implicit fabricated imputation.

statement: Numerator, denominator, comparison periods, and dimensions must use compatible time scopes.
validation_rule: Reject mismatched periods unless the comparison explicitly requires them.

statement: A calculation that divides by a denominator requires a nonzero, defined denominator.
validation_rule: If denominator is zero/null, return undefined/not available rather than infinity or fabricated zero.

statement: Period-over-period growth requires comparable current and previous values and a nonzero previous value.
validation_rule: Previous != 0; period definitions match.

statement: Standard CAGR requires valid start/end values and a positive number of periods.
validation_rule: Starting > 0 and N > 0 for standard real-valued formula; disclose period unit.

statement: NPS must be computed from the same survey population and fall within its theoretical range.
validation_rule: Each percentage in [0,100]; NPS in [-100,100].

statement: The constant-retention CLV formula is valid only when margin, retention, and discount rate use the same period and its simplifying assumptions are acceptable.
validation_rule: 0 <= retention <= 1; denominator > 0; same periodicity; assumptions disclosed.

statement: Price-elasticity inputs must compare compatible conditions and identify the estimation basis.
validation_rule: No elasticity claim from unmatched periods/products without caveat.

statement: The linear optimal-price formula requires a linear demand function and defined maximum reservation price and variable cost.
validation_rule: If linear-demand assumption is unsupported, do not apply the formula.

statement: NPV cash flows and discount rate must share the same period convention.
validation_rule: Align annual/monthly/etc. units; include t=0 exactly once.

statement: IRR should be flagged when nonconventional cash flows can create multiple or misleading roots.
validation_rule: If ambiguous, report NPV and mark IRR not decision-safe.

statement: Productivity numerator and denominator must correspond to the same process and period.
validation_rule: Denominator > 0; label units and factor type.

statement: Utilization requires actual output and design capacity measured on the same output/time basis.
validation_rule: Design capacity > 0; same period and unit.

statement: Reorder-point calculation must align demand-rate units with lead-time units and use only approved safety-stock assumptions.
required_inputs: demand rate; lead time; safety stock
validation_rule: Convert units before calculation; no invented buffer.

statement: Model plans/proposals must parse against the required structured schema before any executable fields are used.
validation_rule: Parsing failure returns controlled error/retry; never infer missing executable values.

statement: Every reported numerical business claim must trace to a verified SQL result or deterministic calculation derived from verified data.
validation_rule: Reject or remove unsupported numerical claims before final response/report.

statement: Project definitions/formulas retrieved from CSV knowledge must preserve source metadata and approval status.
validation_rule: Use only approved/provisional rows according to policy; preserve source title/page in audit/report when material.

statement: Repair retries are limited and may not weaken security rules.
validation_rule: Max retries = 2; security rejections terminate/return safe status.

statement: When local-only mode is enabled, the model endpoint must resolve to an approved localhost Ollama host.
validation_rule: Allow only configured localhost/127.0.0.1 endpoint; reject cloud model URLs.

statement: Secrets must not appear in model context, logs, reports, or user-visible exception text.
validation_rule: Detect/redact known credential fields; never echo `.env` contents.

statement: Generated report paths must resolve under the approved reports/output directory.
validation_rule: Canonical resolved path must have approved base as parent.

statement: Every chart value must come from the verified DataFrame used for the answer/report.
validation_rule: Compare chart source frame to verified result frame/hash or direct object lineage.

statement: Every report metric must be traceable to executed SQL and/or deterministic calculation, with run metadata.
required_inputs: report values; run id; SQL/calculation provenance
validation_rule: No orphan number in report; include method/provenance section.

statement: The final answer should distinguish verified facts, calculations, assumptions, and interpretations.
validation_rule: Any unclassified unsupported factual claim is removed or labeled as an assumption/interpretation.

statement: A conclusion requires evidence that is both relevant and sufficient for the claim being made.
validation_rule: If evidence is irrelevant/insufficient, lower the claim or state uncertainty rather than strengthening it rhetorically.
source_title: Critical Thinking Skills For Dummies, 2nd Edition

statement: Known destructive, secret-extraction, prompt-injection, unsupported-data, and path-traversal prompts should remain in regression tests.
validation_rule: A regression passes only when unsafe effect is prevented and no sensitive content leaks.
